summary.text: One of the last courses from the design stable of Seve Ballesteros, opened in January 2012 on Portugal's Silver Coast.

setting.text: Sits on elevated terrain on the Silver Coast with views across the Óbidos Lagoon and the Atlantic.
Water is in play on eight holes.
Today's Golfer's Kevin Brown counted nine lakes on the course.
On the back nine, six holes meander between lakes linked by cascading streams, and the nine looks out over the Atlantic.
A reviewer on Top100golfcourses said the ocean was in view for about half the round.
A visiting reviewer found wide fairways with few trees, thick and sticky rough, and large, fast greens.
The elevated site is often affected by the prevailing Atlantic winds.
The clubhouse has a glass-fronted veranda upstairs. A Top100golfcourses reviewer said it had a 'Kevin McCloud Grand Designs feel'.

history.text: Opened its tees for play in January 2012.
Seve Ballesteros died before the course came to fruition. NCG says it plays exactly as he wanted.
Premier Golf calls it widely regarded as Ballesteros's final completed design.
A visiting reviewer noted that a display at the resort proudly shows it as the last design by the five-time major champion.
Has hosted the Open de Portugal on the Challenge Tour every year since 2020.
The 2020 Open de Portugal was co-sanctioned by the European Tour and won by Garrick Higgo.
Later winners of the Open de Portugal here: Marcel Schneider (2021), Pierre Pineau (2022, in a playoff), Marco Penge (2023), Matt Oshrine (2024) and J. C. Ritchie (2025).
The Open de Portugal was first played in 1953 and was a European Tour event from 1973 to 2010.

trivia.text: NCG's Top 100 European Golf Resorts list placed Royal Óbidos 39th (page read in October 2026).
Measures nearly 6,700 metres from the tips.
Par 72 made up of five par 3s, eight par 4s and five par 5s.
Today's Golfer's Kevin Brown, writing when it was a year old, said it could prove one of the best courses in Portugal and continental Europe in time.
He also called it 'Seve's parting shot', and said a round fittingly finishes with a pulsating par 5.

1.text: A right-handed dogleg heading north that sets up a run of holes overlooking the Óbidos Lagoon.

2.text: A par 5 and the signature hole in Today's Golfer's view. It plays from an elevated tee in the woods to a sliver of fairway far below, with water down the left, sand on the right and an S-shaped bunker for Seve.
Kevin Brown called it a potential early card wrecker.
A visiting reviewer described a button-hook dogleg left with a pond all the way down the left to a peninsula green, and said it is not worth risking in two.

3.text: A short par 3 with water all around the green. NCG calls it the signature hole of the front nine.
Premier Golf describes it as a par 3 to an island green with the Óbidos Lagoon as a backdrop.

4.text: A Top100golfcourses reviewer called the 4th a long par 4 that demands a very accurate second shot.

5.text: A par 5 of 520 metres that Costa Less Golf calls the feature hole of the front nine. The approach goes to a large, undulating green surrounded on three sides by water.

6.text: A par 3 played across water. NCG says it is even shorter than the 3rd, yet plenty of balls end up in the lagoon short of the green.

7.text: A Top100golfcourses reviewer called it a long par 5 with commanding views over the lagoon.

11.text: A Top100golfcourses reviewer called it a huge par 5 with water.

A visiting reviewer described a short par 5 where the second shot is downhill over a large pond, with a layup left of the water leaving a short chip to a green that slopes severely from back to front.

12.text: A par 4 of 420 metres that Costa Less Golf calls the highlight of the back nine. Both the drive and the second shot must go between and over two lakes and a curving stream.

18.text: A par 5 of almost 600 yards from the back tees. NCG calls it the highlight of the back nine, with a panoramic view over the nine, the clubhouse and the Atlantic.

local.text: Neighbours the West Cliffs resort and sits among a cluster of Silver Coast courses.
Praia D'El Rey is about nine minutes away.
The nearest major airport is Lisbon.
The medieval walled town of Óbidos is nearby, and a local drink is ginja cherry liqueur, often served in a chocolate cup.
Óbidos is known as the Town of Queens. Tradition says King Dinis gave it to Queen Isabel, and later queens held it as part of their household.
The castle inside the walls has housed one of Portugal's first historic inns since 1951.
The town walls run for 1,565 metres, and an aqueduct about 3km long, built in 1573 by Queen Catherine, can be seen from the walls.
Óbidos hosts a Medieval Fair and an International Chocolate Festival, and has UNESCO recognition as a Creative City of Literature.
